annotation.title_clean: Cloud Robotics Law and Regulation: Challenges in the Governance of Complex and Dynamic Cyber-Physical Ecosystems
annotation.title_en: Cloud Robotics Law and Regulation: Challenges in the Governance of Complex and Dynamic Cyber-Physical Ecosystems
annotation.venue: QMUL Cloud Legal Project / SSRN working paper
annotation.summary_en: Working paper analysing legal and regulatory challenges of cloud robotics, where physical robots depend on cloud services. It finds a fragmented EU framework (product safety, liability, GDPR), difficulty attributing responsibility among multiple parties, unclear data controller roles, and a need to balance private standards with public law-making.
key_provisions_or_claims: Regulation of cloud robotics is fragmented, pieced together from product safety, machinery, medical device, toy and GDPR rules.
EU product liability distinguishes products from services, which sits poorly with hybrid robot-cloud ecosystems.
Attributing liability among multiple parties in cloud robotics ecosystems is difficult.
Identifying data controllers and processors, transparency and data portability are unclear in cloud robotics.
Balance needed between private standard-setting and public law-making.
